prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external-processing except interfaces. Mission Control Center(Bluebell):command authority/release; elevated access requires approved shift-role/time-limit. Mission Planning System(Cedar)→Contact booking requests→Ground Network Manager(Juniper),metadata/command preparation package→Payload Processing Facility(Forgehouse)/Bluebell; Laser Retroreflector Window scheduling constrained. Juniper→Antenna Deicing Notice→Spacecraft Operations Team. Command Validation Gateway(Osprey):independent validation; mask file integrity/configuration/operator-approval must match security baseline; maneuvers require screening/concurrence. Telemetry Ingest Service validates/isolates/stages→Pass Replay Packet→Spacecraft Operations Team verifies archived-context anomaly reconstruction. Network Control System(Lantern):approved routing/logged changes; Security Exception Ticket restricts transfers pending containment. North S-Band Antenna/South S-Band Antenna:command/telemetry; Kiruna X-Band Antenna/Svalbard X-Band Antenna:also tracking. Orbit Determination Engine→states/predictions/Doppler Residual Report/Laser Retroreflector Window. Flight Dynamics Team→validated tracking→Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral)→ephemerides/events→Bluebell/Cedar/Forgehouse; Ephemeris Delta Note flags changes. Payload Calibration Team approves baselines/reprocessing. Product Quality Service:provenance/quality/public-status/recorded reprocessing reasons; Product Hold List blocks delivery. Processing versions recorded; baseline changes require comparisons/specification updates. Scheduling service:Primary Processing Cluster→identical Backup Processing Cluster fallback; both unavailable:suspend/preserve staging/notify Bluebell. Recovery:contractual-latency first,then acquisition-order unless approved. Long Term Archive(Granite):authoritative raw/auxiliary/inputs/products/operational-metadata; admission requires Forgehouse package/quality metadata/checksums; persistent identifiers; operational/test/reprocessed distinction. Preserve replaced versions unless policy permits consolidation after comparison-period. Catalogue:baseline/sensing-time/publication-time/quality/replacement relationships; publish via User Services Portal after quality/embargo clearance; review staff-only. Portal:request acceptance/review/search/preview/order/download; scoped access,resumption/integrity/rate-controls. External search/subscriptions/orders/download-status use versioned contracts; restore/publication failure→Portal status/incident-process. Security:least-privilege,strong-authentication,segmentation,continuous-audit. Cybersecurity Desk:predeployment interface

New part:
S213: During triage, operators preserve volatile logs, current configuration state, operator console history, and relevant message identifiers before restarting services or changing routing.
S214: Evidence is stored in write-protected case storage with a chain of custody entry that identifies the collector, collection time, source system, and reason for capture.
S215: Forgehouse must quarantine suspect input and derived output when product lineage cannot be proven during an active anomaly investigation.
S216: Cedar suspends automatic schedule publication when a security or continuity anomaly could invalidate contact commitments or conflict with manual recovery actions.
S217: Continuity modes are declared by the Mission Control Center after consultation with the affected technical leads and are recorded with the operational objective, expected duration, and exit criteria.
S218: In monitor-only mode, command release is stopped, telemetry reception continues where safe, and engineering teams focus on stabilizing observability and protecting evidence.
S219: In essential-service mode, the ground segment prioritizes spacecraft safety contacts, time-critical telemetry capture, core orbit support, and protection of unrecoverable payload data.
S220: Primary Processing Cluster can pause nonessential production queues and reserve compute capacity for validated recovery runs from known-good inputs.
S221: If site degradation persists, processing work is transferred to Backup Processing Cluster only after input custody, software baseline, and operator authorization have been verified.
S222: Cross-site failover is coordinated through Ground Network Manager so that antenna allocation, network routing, firewall state, and contact schedules remain consistent.
S223: North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna are placed in the recovery plan according to current availability and the spacecraft contact priority.
S224: Long Term Archive remains the custody reference during degraded operations, and any delayed ingest or publication is reconciled before normal service status is restored.
S225: User Services Portal communicates confirmed service impacts in operational terms and avoids publishing speculative root cause information before the incident lead approves release.
S226: Recovery is accepted only when command authority is verified, telemetry and product flows are reconciled, security monitoring has returned to the approved baseline, and responsible teams have signed the incident record.
S227: Routine mission service begins only after the operational readiness review confirms that ground procedures, staffing rosters, monitoring views, and escalation paths are under configuration control.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
